original_question: Let B = ⊕_{n≥0} B_n be a semi-graded ring such that B is left noetherian, B_0 is left noetherian and contained in the center Z(B), each homogeneous piece B_n is finitely generated as a left B_0-module, and B satisfies the χ1 condition. If π : sgr-B → qsgr-B is the quotient from finitely generated semi-graded B-modules to the quotient by torsion modules, s is the degree-shift autoequivalence on qsgr-B, and Γ(π(B))_{≥0} := ⊕_{d≥0} Hom_{qsgr-B}(π(B), s^d(π(B))), does there exist an equivalence of categories qgr-B ≃ qgr-Γ(π(B))_{≥0} extending the Serre-Artin-Zhang-Verevkin theorem from finitely graded algebras to semi-graded rings?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in the introduction of arXiv:1908.04880, together with its equivalent reformulation in Proposition 1.2 and the adjoining semi-graded Serre–Artin–Zhang–Verevkin context supplied by Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core mathematical target very well: it uses the semi-graded setting, the four standard hypotheses (left noetherianity of B and B_0, finite generation of each B_n over B_0, and centrality of B_0), the χ1-type finiteness condition, the quotient functor π, the shift s, the section ring Γ(π(B))_{≥0}, and the desired equivalence with qgr on the Γ-side. It also stays tightly focused on the Serre–Artin–Zhang–Verevkin extension problem rather than drifting to neighboring topics in the paper.
missing_details: The paper’s finiteness hypothesis is the semi-graded version of χ1, usually written s-χ1 nearby; to make the question stand-alone, one should spell out that for every finitely generated semi-graded left B-module N and for j=0,1, Ext_B^j(B/B_{≥1},N) is finitely generated as a B_0-module.

The notation qgr/qsgr should be made consistent with the paper: one should explicitly say that qgr-B (or qsgr-B, depending on the local notation adopted) is the quotient of the category of finitely generated semi-graded left B-modules by its torsion subcategory.
One should define B_{≥1}=⊕_{p≥1} B_p, since it appears implicitly in the χ1 condition.
The draft should specify that s is the degree-shift autoequivalence induced on the quotient category by module shifts.

To match the nearby paper context, it helps to mention the canonical graded ring \underline{B}:=⊕_{d≥0}Hom_{sgr-B}(B,s^d(B)), because Proposition 1.2 reformulates the conjecture in terms of the natural map \underline{B}→Γ(π(B))_{≥0}.
The phrase 'extending the Serre-Artin-Zhang-Verevkin theorem' should be sharpened to the exact semi-graded statement asked in the paper, rather than as a broad thematic description.
The draft does not indicate that the equivalence sought is between quotient categories attached to finitely generated objects; this should be explicit on both sides.

If one wants the paper-faithful nearest formulation, the question should be posed as the specific conjectural equivalence for Γ(π(B))_{≥0}, not as a broader inquiry about all possible semi-graded extensions of Serre’s theorem.
refined_question: Let B=⊕_{n≥0}B_n be a semi-graded ring satisfying (C1) B is left noetherian, (C2) B_0 is left noetherian, (C3) each B_n is finitely generated as a left B_0-module, and (C4) B_0⊂Z(B). Assume moreover that B satisfies the semi-graded χ1 condition, namely that for every finitely generated semi-graded left B-module N and for j=0,1, the B_0-module Ext_B^j(B/B_{≥1},N), where B_{≥1}:=⊕_{p≥1}B_p, is finitely generated. If π:sgr-B→qgr-B denotes the quotient from finitely generated semi-graded left B-modules to the quotient by torsion modules, and s is the induced degree-shift autoequivalence on qgr-B, must there exist an equivalence of categories qgr-B ≃ qgr-Γ(π(B))_{≥0}, where Γ(π(B))_{≥0}:=⊕_{d≥0}Hom_{qgr-B}(π(B),s^d(π(B)))?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, with \underline{B}:=⊕_{d≥0}Hom_{sgr-B}(B,s^d(B)), is the natural graded ring homomorphism \underline{B}→Γ(π(B))_{≥0} such that its kernel and cokernel are right bounded, so that Proposition 1.2 reduces the conjectured equivalence qgr-B ≃ qgr-Γ(π(B))_{≥0} to the semi-graded Serre–Artin–Zhang–Verevkin equivalence furnished nearby by Theorem 1.3?
justification: The draft is trying to capture the paper’s Serre–Artin–Zhang–Verevkin problem in the semi-graded setting, and the giveaway is the explicit appearance of Γ(π(B))_{≥0} and the χ1 finiteness condition. Those features point to Conjecture 1.1 as the nearest official target, not to a broader neighboring problem. Proposition 1.2 is relevant because the paper immediately reformulates the conjecture via the canonical map from the semi-graded endomorphism ring \underline{B} to Γ(π(B))_{≥0}. Theorem 1.3 is also essential context because it supplies the semi-graded Artin–Zhang–Verevkin equivalence with the intermediary graded ring, which is precisely why Proposition 1.2 becomes the natural equivalent formulation. Your draft is close, but it should use the semi-graded χ1 hypothesis in its explicit Ext-form, define the quotient category and B_{≥1} carefully, and align the notation qgr/qsgr with the paper’s local setup.
